title: Pointwise cocartesian transport of coherent diagrams
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functor categories, right-pinched mapping spaces and homotopy fibers as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $p:\mathcal E\to\mathcal B$ be a map between quasicategories. Call an edge $u:x\to y$ over $f:p(x)\to p(y)$ cocartesian if, for every $z\in\mathcal E$, the square with top row $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(y,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,z)$ given by precomposition with $u$ and bottom row $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(p(y),p(z))\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal B}(p(x),p(z))$ given by precomposition with $f$ is a homotopy pullback. A homotopy pullback means that the map to the path-space homotopy fiber product is a weak homotopy equivalence. Suppose $p$ is an inner fibration (it lifts all inner horns) and, for every $x\in\mathcal E$, every edge of $\mathcal B$ with source $p(x)$ has a cocartesian lift with source $x$.

For every small simplicial set $K$, postcomposition induces a cocartesian fibration $p_K:\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)$. An edge of its source is $p_K$-cocartesian if and only if its component at every vertex of $K$ is $p$-cocartesian. In particular, for $A:K\to\mathcal E$, $G:K\to\mathcal B$ and a coherent transformation $\eta:pA\to G$, there is a lift $\lambda:A\to\eta_!A$ with $p(\eta_!A)=G$ and cocartesian vertex components. Let $\mathcal F_G=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)}\{G\}$ be the degreewise fiber. For every $H\in\mathcal F_G$, precomposition with $\lambda$ induces a natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F_G}(\eta_!A,H)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{\eta}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(A,H)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal B)}(pA,G)\bigr).$$
Cocartesian lifts compose, and successive transports along composable coherent transformations agree, up to coherent equivalence, with transport along their composite. These equivalences are compatible with the displayed precomposition maps. If $G$ is constant at $b$, the fiber $\mathcal F_G$ is $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E_b)$. The case $K=\Delta^0$ gives the corresponding mapping-space fiber formula for objects of $\mathcal E$. No limits or colimits of $K$-diagrams are assumed.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 3.1.2.1, opposite-category dual (cocartesian exponentiation); Proposition 2.4.4.2 and Proposition 2.4.4.3, duals (mapping fibers and mapping-space criterion); Proposition 2.4.1.7, dual (composition). Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Convert the mapping-space notion in the statement of a cocartesian edge to the horn notion of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] using [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. Its hypotheses hold because $p$ is the given inner fibration and both its source and target are quasicategories. The assumed lifts are therefore horn-cocartesian lifts, so $p$ is a cocartesian fibration in that definition. Let $E^c$ denote $E$ with precisely these cocartesian edges marked. Degenerate edges are cocartesian by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], so this is a marking. The lifting characterization [lem-coef-infinity-marked-cocartesian-lifting] implies that $E^c\to B^\sharp$ lifts every marked coanodyne map.

source.place: Propositions 2.4.4.3 and 3.1.1.6, duals; Corollary 2.4.1.6, dual. This step changes criteria, not the statement.

proof.text: Use the marked internal Hom of [def-coef-infinity-marked-coanodyne] and form $Q=(E^c)^{K^\flat}$ and $R=(B^\sharp)^{K^\flat}$. Their underlying simplicial sets are $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)$: a marked map $K^\flat\times(\Delta^n)^\flat\to E^c$ is any simplicial map, since marked edges in its domain have both coordinates degenerate. A lifting square from a marked coanodyne $a:U\to U'$ to $Q\to R$ transposes, degree by degree, to a square from $a\mathbin{\square}(\varnothing\to K^\flat)=a\times K^\flat$ to $E^c\to B^\sharp$. Explicitly, $v:T\to W^{K^\flat}$ evaluates to $K\times T\to W$ in degree $m$ by $(k,t)\mapsto v_m(t)_m(k,\operatorname{id}_{[m]})$; the inverse sends an $n$-simplex $t$ to the map $(k,\alpha:[m]\to[n])\mapsto h(k,T(\alpha)t)$. These operations commute with simplicial operators and with markings. To check the needed product assertion, use the pushout-product clause of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus]. Opposite simplicial sets reverse each $n$-simplex vertex order. This sends $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$ and the final marked edge to the initial marked edge; it preserves the triangle-marking and Kan-marking generators and commutes degreewise with products, pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts. Therefore a map is marked coanodyne exactly when its opposite is marked anodyne. Apply the cited theorem to $a^{\mathrm{op}}$ and the degreewise injective map $\varnothing\to(K^\flat)^{\mathrm{op}}$, and reverse again. The result is exactly that $a\times K^\flat$ is marked coanodyne. Step 1 supplies its marked filler. Transposition back gives a filler of the original square. Thus $Q\to R$ has the same lifting property. An edge of $Q$ is marked precisely when its map $K^\flat\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp\to E^c$ is marked, that is, when each vertical edge at a vertex $k$ of $K$ is $p$-cocartesian; these are all the nondegenerate marked edges in this product. Every edge of $R$ is marked.

source.place: Expanded lifting-adjunction argument in the proof of Proposition 3.1.2.1, using Proposition 3.1.2.3, duals; no invocation of 3.1.2.1 as a black box.

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the underlying $Q$ and $R$ are quasicategories for every small simplicial $K$, and their right-pinched mapping spaces are Kan complexes. The marking on $R$ in Step 2 is sharp. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-marked-cocartesian-lifting] to $Q\to R$: its underlying map $p_K$ is a cocartesian fibration, and its cocartesian edges are exactly the marked edges of $Q$, already identified vertexwise in Step 2. Applying [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to the inner fibration $p_K$ expresses this also in the mapping-space convention in the statement. The lifting clause of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] applied to the edge $\eta:pA\to G$ and the source $A$ now gives $\lambda:A\to A'$ over $\eta$. Set $\eta_!A=A'$. Its target lies strictly over $G$, and its vertex components are cocartesian by the criterion just proved. For a degenerate base edge choose the degenerate lift, which is cocartesian by Step 1; this fixes the unit choice before the coherence construction.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.6, dual, applied to the marked internal Hom; Proposition 2.4.4.3, dual. Existence is the defining edge-lifting clause.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal Q=\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$, $\mathcal R=\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)$, $A'=\eta_!A$, and fix $H\in\mathcal F_G$. Put $M'=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Q}(A',H)$, $M=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal Q}(A,H)$, $N'=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal R}(G,G)$, $N=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal R}(pA,G)$. These are Kan complexes by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], the square $M'\to M$ over $N'\xrightarrow{\eta^*}N$ is a homotopy pullback, with its composition homotopy. Both vertical maps are Kan fibrations by [lem-coef-infinity-inner-mapping-fiber], since $p_K$ is inner. The strict fiber $\mathcal F_G$ is a quasicategory: fill each inner horn using $p_K$ over the constant simplex at $G$. In the right-pinched definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], a simplex in the strict fiber of $M'\to N'$ over $1_G$ is a simplex $\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal Q$ with initial face constant at $A'$, last vertex $H$, and entire image in $\mathcal R$ constant at $G$. These are exactly the simplices of $F=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal F_G}(A',H)$, with the same operators. The strict-fiber comparison of [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison], applied to the Kan fibration $M'\to N'$ and $\{1_G\}\to N'$, therefore says that the square $F\to M'$ over $\Delta^0\xrightarrow{1_G}N'$ is a homotopy pullback.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.4.1 and Proposition 2.4.4.3, dual; degreewise calculation of the strict fiber.

proof.text:
Place the two squares of Step 4 side by side, with top row $F\to M'\to M$ and bottom row $\Delta^0\xrightarrow{1_G}N'\xrightarrow{\eta^*}N$. The specified-homotopy pasting assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] applies: the right square and the left square are homotopy pullbacks. Hence the outer rectangle is a homotopy pullback. Its comparison map is exactly
$$F\longrightarrow\operatorname{hofib}_{\eta}(M\longrightarrow N).$$
Here the unit homotopy $\eta^*(1_G)\simeq\eta$ and the square's composition homotopy are concatenated as prescribed by the cited pasting assertion; these unit and composition homotopies are supplied by [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]. Thus the comparison sends $h:A'\to H$ to $h\lambda$ with its specified base path to $\eta$, and is a weak equivalence. This is the displayed formula, with its precomposition map, rather than an unidentified equivalence between its two spaces.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 3.4.1.11 (0110), specified-homotopy pasting, applied at the identity vertex; HTT Proposition 2.4.4.2, cocartesian dual.

proof.text: The formula is natural in $H$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] to $p_K:\mathcal Q\to\mathcal R$ and to the inclusion $\mathcal F_G\to\mathcal Q$, enlarging the containing universe if necessary. Their induced mapping-space maps assemble to coherent natural transformations, whose covariant action is postcomposition. The spine calculus [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] makes the square in Step 4 natural in this variable: for $a:H\to H'$, its comparison is $a(h\lambda)\simeq(ah)\lambda$, with its image under $p_K$ and all higher parameter simplices. Taking the fixed fiber is restriction of these diagrams to the constant identity vertex; the strict-fiber identification is degreewise. The constant-path inclusions of [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] commute with every map of the diagrams, since they insert the constant path at the common image. Consequently the pasted comparison in Step 5 is a coherent natural transformation with precisely these composition paths. Each of its components is an equivalence by Step 5; the componentwise equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes it a natural equivalence of space-valued diagrams.

source.place: Kerodon Corollary 8.3.5.8 (046J), Remark 8.3.5.9, and composition of morphisms (01PF).

proof.text:
Choose two composable coherent base edges $\eta:pA	o G$, $	heta:G	o G'$ together with a base $2$-simplex specifying their composite, and choose the lifts $\lambda:A	o A'$ and $\mu:A'	o A''$ of Step 3. The inner-fibration property of $p_K$ fills their inner $2$-horn over that specified base simplex; call its long edge $
u:A	o A''$. In [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] take $u=\lambda$, $v=\mu$, $w=
u$. The required first-edge hypothesis is $\lambda$ cocartesian. Since $\mu$ is also cocartesian, $
u$ is cocartesian. It and a chosen direct lift $\delta:A	o(	heta\eta)_!A$ are initial objects of $L(A,	heta\eta)$ by the same lemma. The initial-object assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes the full subcategory on these initial lifts a contractible Kan complex. A comparison edge between them retains a triangle $c
u\simeq\delta$ over the degenerate triangle on the long base edge; by the lift lemma $c:A''	o(	heta\eta)_!A$ is an equivalence in $\mathcal F_{G'}$. This proves the successive-transport comparison with its specific triangle, including the identity comparison when a base edge is degenerate.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.1.7, Corollary 2.4.1.6 and Remark 2.4.1.9, duals. In the composition assertion the cocartesian hypothesis is on the first edge lambda.

proof.text: Here are the relative extension data used for higher coherence. Mark the cocartesian edges of $\mathcal Q$ and all edges of $\mathcal R$. Steps 2-3 give a marked map $q:\mathcal Q^c\to\mathcal R^\sharp$ lifting every marked coanodyne. Fix a coherent base simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to\mathcal R$. A string of chosen cocartesian lifts over its consecutive edges is a marked map $(I^n)^\sharp\to\mathcal Q^c$ over $\sigma$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-marked-initial-vertex] to extend it over $(\Delta^n)^\sharp$. Thus the entire lifted simplex, including every composite edge and every higher composition witness, lies over this same $\sigma$. For an $r$-parameter family with its boundary already specified, take $T=\partial\Delta^r$ and $T'=\Delta^r$ in that node's relative parameter clause. The domain is exactly $((\Delta^n)^\sharp\times\partial\Delta^r{}^\flat)\amalg_{(I^n)^\sharp\times\partial\Delta^r{}^\flat}((I^n)^\sharp\times\Delta^r{}^\flat)$, so the filler extends the entire family without changing its prescribed spine or its boundary. Consequently the space of completions of a fixed lifted spine over $\sigma$ lifts every boundary, including the empty $r=0$ boundary. The same conclusion holds when only the initial vertex is prescribed. This supplies relative homotopies between choices of lifted base simplices, in arbitrary dimension; it does not try to extract a higher simplex by restricting a $2$-simplex.

source.place: Marked spine/initial-vertex inclusions and Proposition 3.1.2.3, dual, transposed with parameter boundaries. This is the explicit relative lifting problem for coherence.

proof.text: For compatibility among all base simplices, realize the transport data by actual lifted simplices. For $\sigma:\Delta^n\to\mathcal R$ and $A_0\in\mathcal Q$ over $\sigma(0)$, let $\operatorname{Lift}(\sigma,A_0)$ have as $r$-simplices the marked maps $(\Delta^n)^\sharp\times(\Delta^r)^\flat\to\mathcal Q^c$ over $\sigma\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$, constant at $A_0$ on $\{0\}\times\Delta^r$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-marked-initial-vertex] to $q$ of Step 8 with $U=\{0\}^\sharp$, $T=\partial\Delta^r$, $T'=\Delta^r$: every $\partial\Delta^r\to\operatorname{Lift}(\sigma,A_0)$ extends over $\Delta^r$ for all $r\geq0$, so $\operatorname{Lift}(\sigma,A_0)$ is a nonempty contractible Kan complex. With $U=(I^n)^\sharp$ the same holds for lifts with a prescribed spine of chosen transports. All edges of a lift are marked, hence $p_K$-cocartesian. An operator $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ restricts a lift over $\sigma$ to a lift over $\sigma\alpha$ starting at its vertex $\alpha(0)$, strictly compatibly with composition; so lifts over all base simplices and faces form one simplicial system and nothing chosen independently is glued. Over a $2$-simplex with spine $\eta,\theta$ a lift with spine $(\lambda,\mu)$ is a triangle $(\lambda,\mu,\nu)$ of Step 7; degenerate lifts (Step 3) give the units, and lifts over higher simplices give associativity and all higher data, each in a contractible space. The direct lift $\delta$ and $\nu$ are initial in $L(A,\theta\eta)$ by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality], and by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] their comparisons with lift triangle form a contractible Kan complex, mapped to one another by face restriction. Thus the Step 7 comparisons extend, up to contractible choice, to a coherent system of lifted simplices over their specified base simplices.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.2.3, dual, applied to the marked initial-vertex and spine inclusions of Step 8 with parameter boundaries; Proposition 2.4.1.7 and Corollary 2.4.1.6, duals, for the initial lifts. No straightening is invoked.

proof.text:
These comparisons respect the mapping formula. Use the notation of Step 7: $\lambda:A	o A'$, $\mu:A'	o A''$, their long edge $
u$, a direct lift $\delta:A	o(	heta\eta)_!A$, and the comparison $c:A''	o(	heta\eta)_!A$ with its triangle $c
u\simeq\delta$. For $h:(	heta\eta)_!A	o H$ in the final fiber, [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine] gives
$$h\delta\simeq(hc)
u\simeq((hc)\mu)\lambda.$$
The base of this homotopy is the specified composite triangle for $	heta\eta$, because the lifted triangle lies over it. More generally apply the mapping-square criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to $\lambda$ and a test object over $G'$. Paste with the path-space fiber over $	heta:G	o G'$ by [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting], exactly as in Steps 4-5. This identifies the fiber at $	heta$ with the fiber at $	heta\eta$; using the formula for $\mu$ gives successive precomposition. Thus the displayed homotopy is a homotopy of the required fiber maps. For every higher comparison of Step 9, the spine calculus and the coherent Hom-functoriality of [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] carry its faces and degeneracies to the corresponding higher homotopies of precomposition, including their images under $p_K$. The constant-path comparisons used in Steps 4-6 commute with these maps. This proves compatibility in the space-valued natural equivalences, including units and all higher composition data.

source.place: HTT Propositions 2.4.4.2-2.4.4.3, duals, and Kerodon 0110, 01PF and 046J: the specified triangles give the compatibility maps.

proof.text: If $G$ is constant at $b$, an $n$-simplex of $\mathcal F_G$ is exactly a map $K\times\Delta^n\to E$ whose image under $p$ is the constant map at $b$. Such maps are precisely the maps $K\times\Delta^n\to E_b$; precomposition with simplicial operators is identical on both sides. Hence $\mathcal F_G=\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_b)$ degreewise. For $K=\Delta^0$ the same definitions identify $p_K$ with $p$ and the formula of Step 5 with the object-level formula. For $K=\varnothing$, both functor simplicial sets and the relevant fiber are a point, and the formula identifies points. No step used a limit or colimit of a $K$-diagram.
